findings.title: Invalidate local recovery codes after external regeneration
findings.failure_scenario: A federated user with existing local recovery codes regenerates them after their storage provider gains recovery-code support. Successful external creation leaves the local credential intact, so an old code rejected by external storage still authenticates through the local validator.
findings.suggested_fix: After successful external creation, remove existing locally stored recovery-code credentials so regeneration invalidates the previous set.
findings.evidence: CredentialHelper.java:125-129 bypasses RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.createCredential, whose lines 39-42 remove the previous local credential. UserCredentialManager.java:70-80 retains externally rejected inputs for local validation, and RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.java:105-118 accepts matching old local codes.

findings.title: Consume recovery codes when the test provider validates them
findings.failure_scenario: After a successful federated recovery-code login, the provider retains every code and accepts the same code on subsequent logins. Its credential enumeration reconstructs the original full list, so the browser keeps requesting the first code and exhaustion never triggers regeneration.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate only the next unused recovery code, persist its consumption, and expose the remaining credential state from getCredentials.
findings.evidence: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:340 returns an anyMatch result without updating stored codes, while lines 237-241 reconstruct all original codes on every read. The local provider at RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.java:111-118 validates the next code, removes it, and persists the updated credential.
